title: Home Loan EMI Paid? Don't Forget These Crucial Documents
description: Once your home loan is fully repaid, collecting specific documents from your bank is a critical final step. The 'No Dues Certificate' and the original propert.

faq.q: What is a No Dues Certificate and why is it important?
faq.a: A No Dues Certificate (NDC) is an official document from your lender confirming that you have fully repaid your loan and have no outstanding dues. It's crucial as legal proof that the debt is cleared and the bank has no further claim on your property.

faq.q: How long does the bank have to return my property documents?
faq.a: As per RBI guidelines, banks must return all original property documents within 30 days of receiving the full repayment of the loan.

faq.q: What if the bank delays returning my documents?
faq.a: If the bank fails to return the documents within 30 days, they are liable to pay a compensation of ₹5,000 for each day of delay to the borrower.

faq.q: Do I need to update my CIBIL report after loan closure?
faq.a: Yes, it is highly recommended to check your CIBIL report a few weeks after loan closure to ensure the loan status is updated to "Closed." This prevents any negative impact on your credit score and future borrowing capacity.

faq.q: What is a Deed of Reconveyance?
faq.a: A Deed of Reconveyance (or Mortgage Release Deed) is a legal document registered with the Sub-Registrar's office that formally removes the bank's charge or lien on your property from public records, establishing your clear title. It's required in some states.

faq.q: What should I do if the bank claims to have lost my original documents?
faq.a: If the bank loses your original documents, they are legally obligated to help you obtain duplicate copies and bear all associated costs, including advertising in newspapers and obtaining certified copies. You can also claim compensation for the delay as per RBI norms.
